title: Bare HH:MM:SS in front matter silently becomes an integer (YAML 1.1 sexagesimal)

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Found reviewing kanbus-dacb70. PRE-EXISTING PyYAML behavior, not introduced by that fix, but it defeats part of it.

REPRO:
  front matter:  t: 13:30:00
  markus ast ->  "t": 48600

CAUSE: PyYAML implements YAML 1.1, where bare HH:MM:SS is a SEXAGESIMAL INTEGER literal, not a time. 13*3600 + 30*60 = 48600. The value is converted to a meaningless int by the YAML loader BEFORE any Markus code sees it.

TWO CONSEQUENCES:
1. SILENT DATA CORRUPTION. A publication time in front matter becomes a nonsense integer with no error at all. This is the exact failure class kanbus-dacb70 was told to avoid - it is arguably worse than the crash that bug fixed, because it is silent. Newsroom content has publication times; this will bite.
2. The datetime.time branch of _to_json_safe added in kanbus-dacb70 (e374323) is effectively DEAD CODE for YAML front matter, since PyYAML never produces a datetime.time from a bare HH:MM:SS. Worth confirming and either removing it or making it reachable.

NOTE date is unaffected: 'when: 2026-09-04' correctly yields datetime.date and now serializes to ISO 8601. Only bare times are affected.

FIX DIRECTIONS (decide deliberately, this is a contract question):
(a) Use a YAML 1.2 core-schema loader (e.g. ruamel.yaml in 1.2 mode), where sexagesimals are gone and 13:30:00 stays a string. Cleanest semantics; check blast radius on existing front matter.
(b) Keep PyYAML but install a resolver that removes the sexagesimal int pattern.
(c) Document that times must be quoted, and detect the ambiguous pattern to raise a clear error rather than silently coercing.

(a) or (b) preferred - option (c) still relies on authors remembering. Whatever is chosen, add behave coverage.
